answer: Each agent identity must post its own bond, refunded only after a long graded history. An attacker splitting into a thousand sybils must post that bond a thousand times, so marginal cost never falls with volume and payoff stays sublinear. Tenure acts as an anchor: a young alias with no track record earns almost nothing, so spend cannot be recouped quickly. Grading peers attest only coherent answers, working like a prism separating real reasoning from text a script tried to forge. Over a long horizon, honest agents amortise their bond while fake identities keep paying fresh stakes.
